trust_decision.summary: Whether a template string may execute OS-touching functions is decided by whichever code calls template.Render: the renderer trusts every string it is given and binds the single shared func map (cmd/readFile/stat/glob/env/expandenv), so the real decision is 'is this text user-authored config?' and path.setStyle answers it wrongly for a string composed from raw filesystem folder names.

landing_point.why: The advisory names the path segment; this is the only place where text built from filesystem folder names (pt.Path, filled at src/segments/path.go:251-282 from pt.root/pt.relative, which come from pt.env.Pwd() at src/segments/path.go:185-196) is fed back into template.Render with the full func map, so a directory named after a template expression executes cmd.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The shared template package is generic plumbing with twenty trusted callers, so a solver can argue the bug is the Path segment's misuse of Render rather than the renderer's func map (and its cache key), and fix only the caller.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Config-authored template values that end up inside pt.Path must keep resolving through the setStyle re-render: mapped_locations values are spliced into root/relative unrendered (pt.mappedLocations[key] at src/segments/path.go:738 and :762-777) and only get executed by the render at :285, and a folder name that literally contains '{{ cmd `whoami` }}' must still be printed verbatim rather than stripped or escaped away (fix.diff:238). A fix that drops the re-render or blanket-escapes braces in pt.Path breaks the first, and one that deletes template markers from folder names breaks the second.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: render the substituted branch text (mapped_branches value) as a template, not just the config branch_template
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: branch names arrive from repository metadata; a maintainer wanting to theme 'feature/xyz' would re-render the composed branch text exactly as setStyle re-renders pt.Path.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: format l.Version into version_url_template before rendering it
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the version is parsed from tool output, and building the URL by interpolating the version into the template string is the natural next refactor in buildVersionURL.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second render of the already-resolved url option
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the segment resolves the url and then uses it; a 'resolve templates twice in case the first pass produced more' helper is the same shape as setStyle.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: options.Map.Template called on an option populated at runtime (refreshed access token, cached API value)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the helper renders any option value with the full func map and documents that as its purpose; nothing distinguishes a config-authored value from one a segment filled in.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: RenderUntrusted that shares a cached parse with the full func map because the key has no trust bit
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the guard then silently fails whenever the same text was first rendered trusted; the published fix had to change precisely this key.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: pooled Text reused across trust levels leaving a stale trusted flag
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the pool hands objects between renders, so forgetting to reset the flag in release() flips a later untrusted render back to the full func map.

O9_family: template injection (CWE-1336) leading to arbitrary OS command execution (CWE-94) via the text/template func map
